questions.text: In which country/city can you find this famous statue?
questions.funFact: Christ the Redeemer stands 30 meters tall and was completed in 1931. It is an Art Deco statue of Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, created by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and built by Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa, in collaboration with French engineer Albert Caquot and Romanian sculptor Gheorghe Leonida who sculpted the face.

questions.text: This flaming crater is known as the 'Door to Hell'. Where is it?
questions.funFact: The Darvaza gas crater has been burning continuously since 1971.

questions.text: This iconic mountain is a symbol of which country?
questions.funFact: Mount Fuji is 3,776 meters high and last erupted in 1707.

questions.text: This colorful town with blue and white houses is in which country?
questions.funFact: Sidi Bou Said's blue and white color scheme was established by a French baron in 1915.

questions.text: This glass noodle stir-fry dish called Japchae is from which country?
questions.funFact: Japchae was originally created for a royal banquet in the 17th century in Korea.

questions.text: Fish and chips is a beloved national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: The first fish and chip shop in the UK opened in the 1860s.

questions.text: This tagine dish with chicken and olives is from which country?
questions.funFact: The tagine is both the name of the dish and the conical clay pot it's cooked in.

questions.text: This communal hot pot is a traditional way of eating in which country?
questions.funFact: Hot pot has been a Chinese tradition for over 1,000 years, especially popular in Sichuan.

questions.text: The Day of the Dead (Dia de los Muertos) is celebrated in which country?
questions.funFact: Day of the Dead is a celebration of life and death, with roots in Aztec tradition.

questions.text: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, originated in which country?
questions.funFact: Diwali is celebrated by over 1 billion people worldwide across multiple religions.

questions.text: The Haka is a traditional war dance of which indigenous people?
questions.funFact: The All Blacks rugby team famously performs the Haka before every match.

questions.text: The colorful kente cloth is traditionally woven by which people?
questions.funFact: Kente cloth patterns have specific meanings and were once reserved for royalty.

questions.text: The sari is a traditional draped garment from which country?
questions.funFact: The sari has been worn for over 5,000 years, making it one of the oldest garments.

questions.text: The hanbok is the traditional clothing of which country?
questions.funFact: Hanbok is characterized by vibrant colors and simple lines without pockets.

questions.text: The poncho is a traditional garment originating from which region?
questions.funFact: The poncho has been worn by indigenous peoples of the Andes for over 500 years.

questions.text: Which country won the very first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.funFact: Uruguay hosted and won the first ever World Cup in 1930, beating Argentina 4-2 in the final in Montevideo.

questions.text: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
questions.funFact: Brazil has won the World Cup 5 times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002) — more than any other nation.

questions.text: Which African country was the first to reach a World Cup quarter-final?
questions.funFact: Cameroon reached the quarter-finals at Italia 1990, led by 38-year-old Roger Milla, becoming the first African team to go that far.

questions.text: Which Colombian singer is known for the hits 'Hips Don't Lie' and 'Dai Dai'?
questions.funFact: Shakira's 'Waka Waka' was the official song of the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa. She sings in both Spanish and English.

questions.text: Which South Korean group performed the worldwide hit 'Dynamite'?
questions.funFact: BTS (Bangtan Sonyeondan) became the first South Korean act to top the US Billboard Hot 100. Their fan base is called the 'ARMY'.

questions.text: Which Lebanese singer is famous for the song 'Habibi Ya Nour El Ain'?
questions.funFact: Amr Diab is Egyptian, often called the 'Father of Mediterranean Music'. 'Habibi Ya Nour El Ain' (1996) became one of the best-selling Arabic songs of all time.

questions.text: ⚡ SCORE DOUBLE — Where is Ericsson's Headquarters? Drop a pin!
questions.funFact: Ericsson was founded in 1876 and is headquartered in Kista, Stockholm.

questions.text: ⚡ SCORE DOUBLE — Since what year has Ericsson been established in France?
questions.funFact: Following the fire at the Gutenberg telephone station in Paris in 1908, Ericsson established its presence in France in 1909.

questions.text: ⚡ SCORE DOUBLE — When did the Ericsson France R&D center open?
questions.funFact: The Ericsson France R&D center opened its doors in 2020.

questions.text: ⚡ SCORE DOUBLE — How many floors are open in Ericsson Massy?
questions.funFact: The Ericsson Massy building has 4 floors plus the ground floor (RDC) open.

questions.text: ⚡ SCORE DOUBLE — How many nationalities are represented at Ericsson France?
questions.funFact: Ericsson France has 45 nationalities across the company, and the R&D center (ESF) alone has 31 different nationalities!
